topic: Operator Precedence and Associativity in C++ Expressions
explanation: Operator precedence and associativity are fundamental concepts in C++ that determine the order in which operators in an expression are evaluated. Precedence dictates which operators are applied first (e.g., multiplication before addition), while associativity handles the direction for operators of the same precedence (e.g., left-to-right for most arithmetic operators). In real-world programming, this is crucial for writing reliable code, especially in mathematical computations, algorithm implementations, or financial calculations where subtle errors can lead to incorrect results. Best practices include using parentheses to explicitly group operations, making code more readable and less error-prone. Common pitfalls include assuming a left-to-right evaluation for all operators or ignoring precedence rules, which can cause bugs; to avoid them, always consult operator precedence tables and write clear, explicit code.
